text.p: Police seized nearly 450 pounds (20 kg) of cocaine in a raid on a rebel-controlled drug "fortress" in Colombia's southwestern jungle, authorities said on Saturday.

"It was a cocaine-producing fortress guarded by FARC guerrillas," National Police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano said of the clandestine drug complex that elite anti-drug agents raided on Friday in Guaviare Province.

Serrano said a police sergeant was killed as scores of agents, backed by army troops and helicopter gunships, fought their way into the facility, which was surrounded by rebels of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).

The sprawling drug factory, which consisted of three separate laboratories for processing cocaine, was surrounded by guerrilla encampments believed to have housed up to 120 men, all of whom managed to melt back into the surrounding jungle after the raid began, Serrano told Reuters.
He estimated that the three laboratories were capable of producing up to three tons of cocaine a week and said that more than 9 million gallons of precursor chemicals were destroyed at the site.

In other developments, Serrano said one policeman and three civilians were killed in an overnight attack by FARC rebels on Venecia, a small town in a mountainous area about 40 miles (60 km) southwest of Bogota.
The rebels destroyed the town's old police headquarters and a new one still under construction, and the dead included a bank manager who refused to open his bank's safe to the rebels, Serrano said.

The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest rebel group, was formed as a pro-Soviet Marxist group in 1964. Authorities say it specializes in kidnappings and the protection of rural drug farms and laboratories.
